trust_decision.summary: sanitize_css_source decides whether user-written theme CSS may keep a url()/@import that makes the rendering browser fetch an external resource; it applies a regex blocklist to the raw text without first resolving CSS escapes, so escaped keywords (e.g. an escaped 'u' in url) pass.

landing_point.why: The summary names the 'CSS sanitizer' for report themes; sanitize_css_source is the only CSS sanitizer and its docstring names the SSRF/outbound-request goal.

fix_sites.entry_point: POST /api/themes (backend/main.py:642) via ThemeCreate.custom_css validator (backend/schemas.py:320-323); also POST /api/database/import (backend/main.py:969, call at backend/main.py:1038-1039) and GET /api/themes response re-validation via ThemeResponse(ThemeBase) (backend/main.py:637, backend/schemas.py:330)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: The save/reload route (database import, backend/main.py:1037-1039) and the response schema (backend/schemas.py:330) both call the same sanitize_css_source, so the one-function fix covers them automatically; no separate site exists that needed its own change.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: image-set("http://...") strings carry no url() token and are not an escape-encoding trick, so a solver can argue the report is only about CSS escapes and that image-set is a separate CSS feature that the url() blocklist never covered.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: url(data:...) and url(#fragment) must survive (asserted by the existing test), and ordinary CSS such as content:"\2014" escapes and plain rules must be kept; an over-broad fix (drop every url(), reject any backslash, or wipe the whole stylesheet) breaks this.

O6_input_shapes: hex escape \XX with 1-6 hex digits plus optional trailing whitespace (fix.diff:154)
single-character literal escape \X, including a newline (fix.diff:155)
applies to url(, @import, expression(, javascript:/vbscript:, -moz-binding, behavior once decoded (backend/schemas.py:281-291)

O7_producer.where: backend/schemas.py:320-323 (ThemeBase.custom_css validator, inherited by ThemeResponse at backend/schemas.py:330)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: CSS image-set()/-webkit-image-set() take bare string URLs with no url() token, so the url() allowlist never sees them and the browser still fetches the external image
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Not an escape bypass; the report's mechanism is escape decoding, and the docstring lists only url()/@import as the fetch routes (backend/schemas.py:272-273).

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a client-side CSS clean-up in injectThemeStyles (or in the HTML-export builder) that strips url() on raw text before the browser tokenises it
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The CSS is assembled into a <style> on the client; a maintainer could plausibly add defence in depth there with the same naive regex.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: the import path running its own inline url()/@import regex instead of calling sanitize_css_source
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The import block already re-implements the image sanitising separately (backend/main.py:1005-1021); a second CSS copy at a distance would fit that style.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: widening _CSS_VALUE_RE for theme vars to accept quotes/colons/backslash so vars can carry image-set or escaped url values
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Theme vars are written into the same <style> (js/app.js:1720-1721); allowing richer values such as gradients or fonts is a natural feature request.

O9_family: input canonicalisation / blocklist-before-decode (CWE-180) leading to forced outbound requests (CSS-based SSRF/tracking in the rendering browser)

O10_build.toolchain: pip install -r requirements.txt (fastapi, pydantic v2, sqlalchemy, pytest); unpinned versions at the pinned commit
O10_build.project_tests: backend/tests/test_pro_features.py:32-64 (theme vars and custom_css sanitisation via TestClient); hidden tests can call schemas.sanitize_css_source directly or POST /api/themes

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add a case-insensitive regex for an escaped 'u' (\75) in front of the url() check, or reject backslashes outright, leaving other escape spellings and image-set() strings open.

out_of_scope_notes: The first fix commit (714e05e, username allowlist + deleteUser handler + dependency bumps) is already present at the pinned commit (backend/schemas.py:11-12, 60-68), so it is not part of this advisory's diff in effect.
The theme editor's live preview injects unsanitised customCss into the page before save (js/app.js:1846-1854); this is self-only, so not pursued.
The published decoder decodes escapes inside CSS strings too (e.g. an escaped quote becomes a bare quote), which can alter legitimate content strings; this is a fix-quality note, not a route.
